tools_used: provisioned documents (questions-presented, petition, brief-in-opposition + bundled respondent merits brief)
helpful: The statpack merits section's per-Term disturbed/parsed table made the strictly-prior pooling arithmetic trivial, and its excluded column made quotability checkable in place.
The provisioned brief-in-opposition file bundling the respondent's merits brief was the single most valuable input for a grant-moment merits cell — real merits advocacy, not just the docket skeleton.
gaps: The petitioner's merits brief (filed 2026-06-08) was on the docket but not provisioned, so the merits advocacy I saw was one-sided toward the respondent; a merits-stage cell would benefit from the document pipeline fetching both merits briefs once filed.
A citation-filtered fedcourts query cost ~348 MB of ranged reads to return zero rows; a cheap existence check on the sparse citation column before the scan would save that egress.
Amicus briefs are docket entries only — even a party-alignment line (supporting petitioner/respondent/neither) in the snapshot would help read the merits posture.
notes: Forward merits cell at the grant moment; anchored on the statpack merits pool (69.7%) and adjusted to 0.72. The documents.json 'brief-in-opposition' entry is really a two-document bundle (BIO + respondent merits brief) — helpful, but the kind label under-describes it; flagged as info-level data-quality.
